name: Hanging Knee Raise
description: The hanging knee raise is a beginner-to-intermediate hanging core exercise in which the athlete draws both knees toward the chest while hanging from a bar. By reducing the lever arm compared to straight-leg variations, it makes hip flexor and rectus abdominis training accessible to those building toward hanging leg raises and toes-to-bar. Proper posterior pelvic tilt during the top of the movement ensures abdominal engagement beyond mere hip flexion.

execution.starting_position: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip at shoulder-width. Arms fully extended, body still.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a secure overhead bar. Strive for a stable dead hang before initiating the movement.
steps: Step 1: Begin in a stable dead hang with arms fully extended.
Step 2: Brace the core and draw both knees upward toward the chest.
Step 3: At the top, tuck the pelvis posteriorly and compress the abs to ensure the rectus abdominis is loaded.
Step 4: Lower the knees with control back to the starting position.
Step 5: Avoid swinging at the bottom — pause briefly in dead hang before the next repetition.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as the knees rise. Inhale on the controlled descent.
common_mistakes: Swinging the body to generate momentum rather than using core strength
Dropping the knees too fast — the eccentric phase should be controlled
Failing to posteriorly tilt the pelvis at the top, leaving the movement as pure hip flexion
safety_considerations: Grip strength limits many beginners — use chalk or straps if needed.
Avoid swinging as it places uneven load on the shoulder joints.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Knees should rise to at least hip height; ideally toward the chest for maximum abdominal involvement.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2-0-2: 2 seconds concentric, 2 seconds eccentric. Eliminate momentum.
coaching_cues: Pull your knees into your belly
Round the lower back at the top — don't just lift legs
Pause at the bottom — no swinging
